sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the blocks immediately west of the West Shore Railroad in central Dumont, between Dixon Avenue at the top and Niagara Street at the bottom, with Johnson Avenue along the left edge and Cortland Avenue running diagonally beside the tracks on the right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows four tiers of blocks. The northern block between Dixon and Roosevelt Avenues is largely vacant, with a row of two-storey frame dwellings fronting Roosevelt. The blocks along Roosevelt and McKinley Avenues are residential, almost entirely two-storey frame dwellings with small auto houses behind. The block between McKinley and West Madison Avenues holds the First M.E. Church and, at its east end near the railroad, a row of brick and concrete-block stores and an office. South of West Madison Avenue stands the 104th Engineers N.J. National Guard Armory, a tile building with drill hall, among dwellings, offices and small stores; the block between it and Niagara Street is residential with concrete-block garages. Cortland Avenue jogs at West Madison Avenue, the northern section lying further west than the southern. East of Cortland lie the multiple tracks of the West Shore Railroad with the Dumont passenger depot, a subway entrance and a pedestrian subway under the tracks, and a long frame platform shelter; Railroad Avenue runs along the east side of the tracks at the right edge, and Park Place leaves it at the bottom. Water pipes of 6, 24 and 30 inches are marked in the streets.
notes: Cortland Avenue north of West Madison Avenue is now Veterans Plaza in OpenStreetMap; Cortland Avenue keeps its name south of Madison.
Railroad Avenue east of the tracks corresponds to the modern West Shore Avenue.
The railroad is the West Shore Railroad (W.S.R.R.), with the Dumont depot and a pedestrian subway under the tracks.
Single part, 50 ft. Johnson Av to the West Shore RR between Dixon Av and Niagara: Roosevelt, McKinley, W. Madison, Cortland (now Veterans Plaza north of Madison), depot, armory. Rotation +3 deg.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the business centre of Dumont around the junction of Washington Avenue and Madison Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Railroad Avenue runs along the left edge beside the West Shore Railroad, Washington Avenue crosses the sheet from top to bottom slightly right of centre, New York Avenue forms the top boundary on the east side, and Brook Street (labelled Cooper south of Madison Avenue) runs down the right edge. West Madison Avenue climbs from the railroad to Washington Avenue and continues east as East Madison Avenue; Park Avenue curves down to meet it from the north, and Dumont Avenue and Magnolia Avenue cross the lower right. The west half above Madison is residential, with long narrow lots of frame dwellings between Railroad and Park Avenues and the works of W. S. Mountford, makers of metal goods. Along West Madison Avenue a continuous row of brick and concrete-block stores faces the street, with a hall and bank near Washington Avenue and a vacant garage and bank at the railroad end. South of Madison stand the North Reformed Church and the Fire Department Engine Company No. 1 with its siren, and a row of stores with a plumbing shop and a funeral parlor near Park Place. East of Washington Avenue the blocks hold drug stores, a 32-car garage, an auto repair shop, the police station, a concrete block manufacturer and the Dumont Theatre, a motion picture house. Below Dumont Avenue are an auto printing shop, a contractor's shed with lumber storage and a 35-car garage. Water pipes of 6 to 30 inches are marked in the streets.
notes: Cooper (south of East Madison Avenue) is now part of Brook Street in OpenStreetMap.
Park Place is now Ivy Place; Railroad Avenue corresponds to the modern West Shore Avenue.
Cooper appears to jog east at Dumont Avenue; the Brook Street / Dumont Avenue junction was excluded because it did not fit (7 m).
The fitted rotation (-8.9 degrees) differs by about 12 degrees from sheet 2: the sheets are drawn at different angles.

Single part, 50 ft. Business centre at Washington/Madison: Railroad Av (West Shore Av), Park Av, New York Av, Brook/Cooper (Brook Street), Dumont Av, Magnolia, Park Pl (Ivy Place). Drawn at about -9 deg rotation.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the south-central part of Dumont from Park Place and Magnolia Avenue at the top down to Maple Avenue and the Dumont-Bergenfield borough line at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Railroad Avenue and the single track of the West Shore Railroad run along the left edge, with the railroad freight house and an oil house beside them. Washington Avenue crosses the sheet from top to bottom right of centre. West and East Quackenbush Avenue cross it in the upper third, and Sunnyside and Shadyside Avenues and First Street lie east of Washington Avenue. In the upper left a large open block between Railroad and Park Avenues is marked as a park. Below West Quackenbush Avenue the yard of the Dumont Coal and Lumber Company fills the corner by the railroad, with its office, coal pockets, general storage, lumber piles, lumber storage sheds and a wagon shed; the post office stands next to the company office on Quackenbush Avenue. Further east stands the Dumont High School, a fireproof concrete building with a note that it is to be a grammar school only once the new high school is completed. The rest of the sheet is residential: frame dwellings with auto houses on the blocks east of Washington Avenue along Quackenbush, Sunnyside and Shadyside Avenues, and a few houses on large lots west of Washington Avenue. The southern part of the sheet is largely vacant, and the dash-dot borough line between Dumont and Bergenfield runs along Maple Avenue at the bottom.
notes: First Street is now Short Street in OpenStreetMap.
Maple Avenue (also lettered Maple Street) on the borough line is now Columbia Avenue.
Park Place is now Ivy Place; Railroad Avenue corresponds to West Shore Avenue.
Dumont High School is marked to become a grammar school on completion of a new high school.
Single part, 50 ft. Park Pl to Maple Av (Columbia Av) on the Bergenfield line: Quackenbush, Sunnyside, Shadyside, 1st St (Short Street), Dumont Coal & Lumber, high school.

sheet-5-1.description: The lower and larger part of Sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the northwest residential section of Dumont between Wyandotte Avenue and Manhattan Terrace at the top and Dixon Avenue at the bottom, from Prospect Avenue on the left to Cedar Street on the right. It is separated from the upper part of the sheet by a heavy line. Manhattan Terrace and New Milford Avenue cross the full width; north of New Milford Avenue the cross streets are Maple, Walnut, Hickory, Oak, Fuller (also lettered Elm), Holt (also lettered Chestnut), Pine and Cedar, and south of it Cherokee, Cooper Avenue, Catawba and Johnson Avenue run down to Dakota Avenue. The blocks, numbered 52 to 68, are laid out in narrow lots and are only partly built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings and small auto houses, several of them drawn from plans. The large block east of Johnson Avenue holds the new Dumont High School, built in 1928, with its auditorium and gymnasium wings; the building is of fireproof construction with exposed steel and wood roof, and the note records cinder-block interior walls, concrete floors, electric light and steam heat. The blocks south of Dakota Avenue are vacant, Dixon Avenue along the bottom is marked not open west of Johnson Avenue, and the tracks of the West Shore Railroad touch the lower right corner. Water pipes of 6 inches run in most streets, and the scale bar of 100 feet to an inch is drawn in the lower left.
notes: Maple (north of New Milford Avenue) is now Whittaker Street; Cedar is now Bedford Road; Fuller and Holt keep their names (the alternative names Elm and Chestnut are not in OpenStreetMap).
Dixon Avenue is marked not open west of Johnson Avenue.
Dumont High School, built 1928, drawn from plans.

Two parts, 100 ft, divided by a heavy line: part 1 (lower) Manhattan Terrace to Dixon Av, Prospect to Cedar (Bedford Rd), Dumont High School 1928; part 2 (upper) New Milford line to Prospect Av, Seminole to Seneca.

sheet-5-2.description: The upper part of Sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and separated from the lower part by a heavy line, shows the western edge of Dumont along the New Milford borough line, from Seminole Avenue at the top down to New Milford Avenue and Seneca Avenue, and from the borough line on the left to Prospect Avenue on the right. The dash-dot borough line between New Milford and Dumont runs down the left edge and across the top, with the note to see the map of New Milford beyond it. Lawrence, Lincoln and Lafayette Avenues run north from New Milford Avenue to Moore Avenue and beyond; Iowa Street, Ontario Street and Concord Street lie further east, and Seminole, Wyandotte and Oneida Avenues cross the sheet in two offset sections that jog at Concord Street. The area is a newly laid-out subdivision of narrow lots in numbered blocks 1 to 20, still sparsely built, with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, auto houses and a chicken house. The fuller blocks are those along Lafayette Avenue and Moore Avenue and the blocks east of Concord Street; a small row of stores drawn from plans stands on New Milford Avenue just west of Concord Street. An acoustic fire alarm is marked at Concord Street and New Milford Avenue, and 6-inch water pipes run in the main streets. The north arrow at the dividing line serves both parts of the sheet.
notes: Seminole, Wyandotte and Oneida Avenues jog at Concord Street; OpenStreetMap has two Concord / Seminole nodes about 28 m apart, matching the drawn jog.
Lincoln Avenue is lettered Lincoln (Av.).

Two parts, 100 ft, divided by a heavy line: part 1 (lower) Manhattan Terrace to Dixon Av, Prospect to Cedar (Bedford Rd), Dumont High School 1928; part 2 (upper) New Milford line to Prospect Av, Seminole to Seneca.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the southwest quarter of Dumont from New Milford Avenue at the top to the Bergenfield borough line at the bottom, and from the New Milford borough line on the left to Prospect Avenue on the right. In the upper left, Lawrence, Lincoln and Lafayette Avenues run south from New Milford Avenue, crossed by Morton and Monroe Avenues; this part is built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings and includes the Dumont Fire Department hose house with a pump house, and the Episcopal Church at Ontario Street and Colonial Court. A brook crosses the sheet from the left edge, widening in the centre into a large area marked swamp and pond, around which Concord Street, Bridge Street, Idaho Street and McKinley Avenue end. On the right, between Dixon Avenue and West Madison Avenue along Prospect Avenue, stands the Lincoln Public School. A group of greenhouses with a heater house and a concrete-block greenhouse lies on West Madison Avenue near Lafayette Avenue, where an acoustic fire alarm is marked. South of West Madison Avenue the land is mostly laid out but empty: Dance Boulevard, Aladdin Avenue and Omar run down to the borough line through numbered blocks 215 to 218 with no buildings, a large tract (block 32) holds only a few houses, and Roslyn Avenue has a short row of dwellings. In the lower right, First and Second Streets and Armour Place have dwellings and a row of brick and concrete-block stores at West Madison and Prospect Avenues. The dash-dot borough lines with New Milford and Bergenfield frame the left and bottom, with notes to see the maps of those towns.
notes: McKinley Avenue west of the swamp (at Bridge, Omaha and Idaho) is now Glen Avenue.
Omar (south of West Madison Avenue) is the continuation of Omaha and is now Omaha Street.
Aladdin Avenue / Armour Place was excluded: Armour Place is not drawn at Aladdin Avenue.
Concord / Ontario, Concord / Dixon and Glen (McKinley) / Omaha were rejected at 6 to 12 m; these junctions lie at the edge of the swamp, where the streets ended on the sheet.
Single part, 100 ft. Southwest Dumont: New Milford Av to the Bergenfield line, New Milford line to Prospect Av; swamp and pond, Lincoln School, McKinley (Glen Av) west of the swamp, Omar (Omaha St).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the south-western residential district of Dumont between Prospect Avenue on the left and Cortland Avenue and the West Shore Railroad on the right, from Dixon Avenue at the top down to Maple Avenue and the Bergenfield borough line at the bottom. Roosevelt, McKinley and West Madison Avenues cross the upper half, and below them Niagara Street (also lettered 1st Street), West Quackenbush Avenue (2nd Street), Erie (3rd Street) and Locust Avenue. Cooper Avenue and Johnson Avenue run down the middle of the sheet; in the south, Cooper Avenue, Elm Place, Bergman Terrace, Oakland Avenue and Dick run from Locust Avenue to Maple Avenue. The blocks are lined with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, many with concrete-block auto houses, with a few chicken houses and sheds. Woodside Cemetery fills most of the block between McKinley and West Madison Avenues at Prospect Avenue, with the Independent Hose Company firehouse of the fire department beside it, and baseball grounds occupy the large block south of West Madison Avenue. The northern blocks along Dixon Avenue are only partly built, Dixon Avenue being marked not opened east of Cooper Avenue, and the blocks at the bottom right between Oakland Avenue and Cortland Avenue (260 to 262) are vacant. The large block 257 in the lower left is empty except for houses along Prospect Avenue. The dash-dot borough line with Bergenfield runs along the left edge and the bottom, and the multiple tracks of the West Shore Railroad cross the lower right corner.
notes: Oakland Avenue (south of Erie) is now Johnson Avenue; Elm Place is now Patton Place; Maple Avenue on the borough line is now Columbia Avenue.
Niagara, West Quackenbush Avenue and Erie also carry the old names 1st, 2nd and 3rd Street.
Dixon Avenue is marked not opened east of Cooper Avenue.
Fire Department Independent Hose Company house beside Woodside Cemetery on West Madison Avenue.
Single part, 100 ft. Prospect Av to Cortland/West Shore RR, Dixon Av to Maple Av (Columbia Av); Woodside Cemetery, baseball grounds; Oakland Av = Johnson Av, Elm Pl = Patton Pl.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the northern end of Dumont along the Haworth borough line. New (Massachusetts) Avenue runs across the top of the sheet on the borough line, with the Borough of Haworth beyond it, and Washington Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the top centre. West of Washington Avenue lies a newly laid-out subdivision of Stratford, Harwich and Beverly Roads between Massachusetts and Andover Avenues, divided into numbered blocks 263 to 269 with almost no buildings, and below it a large open tract (71 and 72) with a few scattered dwellings and outbuildings. East of Washington Avenue are Pearl and Pine Streets and Harding Avenue (also lettered Chestnut), crossed by De Long Avenue; the large block 186 between Massachusetts and De Long Avenues is mostly open with a dwelling and several coops. In the lower half Poplar, Larch and Lenox Avenues cross the sheet east of Washington Avenue, with Central Avenue and Fairview Avenue running between them; these blocks are built up with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a stone house and a few small shops, and a split-tire fire alarm is marked at Larch and Fairview Avenues. Gordon Avenue (also lettered Garden Avenue) leaves Washington Avenue at the lower left with a row of houses, and the short Oxford Avenue runs south from Lenox Avenue. Six- and eight-inch water pipes are marked in Washington and Massachusetts Avenues.
notes: Pine (north of Larch Avenue) is now Hazel Street; Fairview Avenue is now Rucereto Avenue.
The Dumont-Haworth borough line runs along Massachusetts Avenue, lettered New (Massachusetts) Avenue.
Residuals of 3 to 4.8 m along Washington and Massachusetts Avenues; De Long / Washington was rejected at 8 m.
Single part, 100 ft. North end on the Haworth line (Massachusetts Av): Stratford/Harwich/Beverly Rds, Washington Av, Pearl, Pine (Hazel St), Harding, Larch, Lenox, Fairview (Rucereto Av).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers north-central Dumont east of the West Shore Railroad, whose multiple tracks cross the left side of the sheet from bottom to top. Washington Avenue runs diagonally from the bottom centre to the upper right, and the sheet extends east to Depew Street. The upper left is a large open tract (blocks 69 and 74) with only a few outbuildings. Below it, between the railroad and Washington Avenue, Manhattan Terrace and New Milford Avenue are joined by the short Summit, Lincoln and Congress Terraces, lined with frame dwellings and a few tile houses. South of New Milford Avenue stand St. Mary's R.C. Church and its rectory, and Park Avenue runs down to Railroad Avenue with rows of dwellings on narrow lots; a tile storage building is near Railroad Avenue at the lower left. East of Washington Avenue the streets form a regular grid: Wood Place, Cresskill, Randolph, Linden (also lettered Park Avenue), Druid, Virginia, Davies and Delaware Avenues cross between Washington Avenue and Depew Street, with Brook, Thompson and Henry Streets running north-south in the lower part. These blocks are partly built up with frame dwellings and a store, Druid Avenue is marked not opened east of Henry Street, and Henry Street is marked not opened. At the bottom New York Avenue meets Washington Avenue, and the Christian Science Society building stands on Washington Avenue near it. An acoustic fire alarm is marked at Virginia Avenue and Washington Avenue.
notes: Manhattan Terrace (east of the railroad) is now West Linden Avenue; Linden Avenue east of Washington Avenue is East Linden Avenue.
Summit Terrace is now Sunset Street; Lincoln Terrace is now American Legion Terrace; Congress Terrace is Congress Street.
Henry Street is marked not opened and is not in OpenStreetMap; Druid Avenue is marked not opened east of Henry.
Washington / Wood Place and Washington / Depew were rejected (8 and 14 m); the modern junctions at the north end of Washington Avenue do not match the drawn ones.
Single part, 100 ft. West Shore RR to Depew St north of New York Av: Manhattan Terrace (W. Linden Av), Summit/Lincoln Ter (Sunset St, American Legion Ter), St Mary R.C. Church.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers eastern Dumont between Lenox Avenue at the top and Delaware Avenue at the bottom, from Depew Street and Washington Avenue on the left to Fairview Avenue and Charles Street on the right. Washington Avenue and Gordon Avenue cut across the upper left corner, and Grant Avenue runs diagonally from Washington Avenue towards the east, where it turns to run straight across the sheet below Fairview Avenue. North of Grant Avenue are Lexington Avenue and the short Oxford Avenue, James Place, Central Avenue and Ormond Place, with frame dwellings, a row of stores on Grant Avenue and, in the upper right, the Dumont Laundry with its boiler and a greenhouse. The Grant Public School stands in block 161 south of Grant Avenue, and the Dumont Hose Company No. 3 firehouse of the fire department faces Fairview Avenue. South of Grant Avenue a regular grid of Wood Place and Cresskill, Randolph, Linden (also lettered Park Avenue), Druid, Virginia and Davies Avenues is crossed by Depew, Howard and Pershing (also lettered Pearl) Streets and Charles Street. The western blocks between Depew and Howard are partly built up with frame dwellings, a few with concrete-block garages and a greenhouse, while the blocks east of Pershing Street (128 to 141) and the large tract 270 along Grant Avenue are laid out in lots but entirely vacant. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets.
notes: Fairview Avenue is now Rucereto Avenue; Pershing (Pearl) is Pershing Street; Linden Avenue is East Linden Avenue.
James Place and Ormond Place are not in OpenStreetMap.
Dumont Laundry with boiler and greenhouse on Lenox Avenue; Grant Public School; Dumont Hose Company No. 3.
Grant Avenue / Howard Street was rejected at 6 m.
Single part, 100 ft. Lenox Av to Delaware Av, Depew to Charles: Grant Av, Grant School, Dumont Laundry; blocks east of Pershing vacant.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the residential district east of Dumont's business centre, between Delaware Avenue at the top and the Bergenfield borough line at the bottom, and from Brook Street (lettered Cooper south of Madison Avenue) on the left to Howard Street on the right. New York, Blauvelt, East Madison and Dumont Avenues, Magnolia Avenue, East Quackenbush Avenue (also lettered Stockholm Avenue) and Marion Avenue cross the sheet, and Thompson and Depew Streets run from top to bottom. The blocks north of Marion Avenue are closely built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, many tile houses along East Quackenbush Avenue and concrete-block garages. Along East Madison Avenue near Brook Street stand an auto repair garage and a filling station with gasoline tanks, and a bowling alley lies on Cooper between Dumont and Magnolia Avenues. Brook Street is marked not opened north of Madison Avenue on its diagonal course towards Delaware Avenue. An acoustic fire alarm is marked on East Madison Avenue at Depew Street. South of Marion Avenue the large block 90 is entirely vacant. In the lower left corner a strip along First Street shows blocks 95, 89, 86 and 87 with frame dwellings on Sunnyside and Shadyside Avenues, and the dash-dot borough line between Dumont and Bergenfield runs along the bottom, where First, Second and Third Streets of Bergenfield are named.
notes: Cooper is now part of Brook Street; First Street (lower left) is now Short Street.
East Quackenbush Avenue is also lettered Stockholm Avenue.
Brook Street north of Madison Avenue is marked not opened 1928.
Delaware / Howard (15 m) and East Quackenbush / Short Street (11 m) were rejected; one of two Brook / Magnolia nodes was rejected.
Single part, 100 ft. Delaware Av to the Bergenfield line, Brook/Cooper to Howard: Thompson, Depew; bowling alley, filling station.

sheet-12-1.description: The main part of Sheet 12, drawn at 200 feet to an inch, covers the eastern edge of Dumont from Massachusetts Avenue on the Haworth borough line at the top down to East Madison Avenue at the bottom, bounded on the right by Knickerbocker Road and the borough lines with Demarest and Cresskill. In the upper half a large subdivision of narrow lots is laid out between Harding Avenue (also lettered Chestnut) and Franklin Street, with Beacon, Pleasant, Whitman, Garfield, Grant and Harrison Streets crossing De Long Avenue (also lettered Lenox Avenue); it is almost entirely vacant. Below it Larch, Laurel, Lenox and Lexington Avenues run east from Fairview and Summit Avenues to Knickerbocker Road, with scattered frame dwellings and a chicken house. Along Grant Avenue lies the yard of Harris Bros. Co., lumber, millwork and plumbing supplies, formerly part of Camp Merritt, with numbered storage sheds, a sash and door works, a parts supply and a print store; further north along Knickerbocker Road stand long buildings marked as former Camp Merritt buildings, now old and dilapidated. The large block 149 south of Grant Avenue is vacant. In the lower part of the sheet, between Delaware Avenue and East Madison Avenue, Charles Street, Grand Avenue, Merritt Avenue (also lettered Washington Avenue) and Wilcott Road run south, crossed by the short Artillery, Liberty and Bayard Places and Rogers Lane, Winslow Place and Austin Road; this area is laid out but holds only a few buildings. Howard Street, New York Avenue and Blauvelt Avenue appear at the lower left. The scale bar of 200 feet to an inch is drawn at the bottom.
notes: Whitman is now the north end of Summit Avenue; Grant Street is now Juniper Street south of Massachusetts Avenue; Fairview Avenue is Rucereto Avenue.
Grand Avenue appears to correspond to Highwood Drive and Wilcott Road to Wolcott Road; Artillery, Liberty and Bayard Places, Rogers Lane, Winslow Place and Austin Road are not in OpenStreetMap.
Former Camp Merritt buildings along Knickerbocker Road, marked old and dilapidated; Harris Bros. Co. lumber yard formerly part of Camp Merritt.
Fit residuals of 3 to 8 m are common on this 200-foot sheet; junctions along De Long Avenue are drawn narrower than today's street.

Two parts, 200 ft: part 1 main map (Massachusetts Av to E. Madison Av along Knickerbocker Rd, Harris Bros lumber, former Camp Merritt buildings); part 2 inset at lower left behind a heavy line (E. Madison Av to Maple Av, Howard to Elm; Levingston = Garden St).

sheet-12-2.description: The inset in the lower left of Sheet 12, set off by a heavy border and drawn at 200 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, shows the south-eastern corner of Dumont between East Madison Avenue at the top and Maple Avenue on the Bergenfield borough line at the bottom, from Howard Street on the left to Elm Street and the Cresskill borough line on the right. Levingston runs diagonally down from East Madison Avenue and then south to the borough line, crossed by Dumont Avenue, Blish Place, Magnolia Avenue and Baker Lane; the short Quackenbush, Marion, Sunnyside and Shadyside Avenues end at Howard Street. Further east Wilcox, Shelby, Chestnut, Clarke and Stanley Streets and Elm Street run south from East Madison Avenue, crossed by Conklin Place and Dunn Place. The area is laid out in large numbered blocks (280 to 297) but is almost empty: a row of small frame dwellings stands on Shelby Street below Baker Lane, a few houses on Stanley Street and Conklin Place, and some scattered dwellings and coops near East Madison Avenue. The dash-dot borough lines with Bergenfield along Maple Avenue and with Cresskill along Elm Street mark the edges of the town.
notes: Levingston is now Garden Street; Maple Avenue on the borough line is now Maple Street.
Magnolia Avenue is drawn 30 ft wide (parcels give 50 ft); street_widths set accordingly.
OpenStreetMap has two Garden Street nodes about 39 m apart at both Magnolia Avenue and Baker Lane, matching the jog of Levingston at Baker Lane.

Two parts, 200 ft: part 1 main map (Massachusetts Av to E. Madison Av along Knickerbocker Rd, Harris Bros lumber, former Camp Merritt buildings); part 2 inset at lower left behind a heavy line (E. Madison Av to Maple Av, Howard to Elm; Levingston = Garden St).
